one_line_contribution: That degradation in self-evolving agent memory is caused by the collection policy — episodes being executed while conditioned on retrieved items, which makes retrieval self-reinforcing and contracts the bank's support — rather than by any property of the written content, demonstrated by a decoupled-collection control (A2) matched on tasks, write path and write count, and extended to a second self-editing channel via a 2x2 with a reflective prompt optimizer plus an instruction/bank transplant.
closest_prior_work: Two threats, one of which the proposal misses entirely. (a) CoEvo-Mem (cited as arXiv 2608.01739) states the identical structural premise; the proposal is right that it is a competing hypothesis rather than a scoop, but a reviewer can fairly read prong 1 as an adversarial ablation of someone else's stated mechanism, which is a modest contribution frame. (b) The one the proposal never cites and that hurts more: degenerate feedback loops in recommender systems — Jiang, Chiappa, Lattimore, Gyorgy, Kohli, 'Degenerate Feedback Loops in Recommender Systems' (AIES 2019), and Chaney, Stewart, Engelhardt, 'How Algorithmic Confounding in Recommendation Systems Increases Homogeneity' (RecSys 2018), plus the exposure-bias line (Mansoury et al. 2020). Those results already establish, formally and empirically, that a system whose future observations are drawn under its own ranking contracts its effective support via preferential attachment, and that randomizing/injecting exploration restores it. B1 (uniform retrieval) and M50 (mixing) are exactly the known fixes from that literature, as is the fresh-data mixing ratio from the model-collapse work the proposal does cite. So the dynamic, the diagnosis and the remedy are all imported; what is genuinely new is the substrate (an append-only text bank retrieved into a frozen model's context, where no weights are updated) and the crossing with a prompt optimizer. That is a real but incremental delta, and the Related Work's framing of the mechanism as previously unidentified overstates it.
strongest_objection: A2 is not a control that isolates 'the collection policy' — it differs from A1 on at least two mundane content pathways that alone predict the entire predicted signature (predictions 1-3), and neither is controlled. (i) Textual copying: in A1 the ExpeL-style distiller is fed a trajectory whose context contained the four retrieved items, so a contracting bank is the expected output of ordinary paraphrase, not of preferential attachment; in A2 the distiller never sees them. Metric (d) would detect the redundancy but cannot attribute it. (ii) Write-set composition: W=40 successful episodes are sampled 'uniformly at random' from successes, and memory plausibly raises success rate most on the five head clusters that already take 65% of draws, so A1's writable pool is head-skewed by construction. Equalizing the write *count* (limitation 3) does not equalize the cluster *composition*, and cluster composition is precisely what effective rank, Gini and cluster coverage measure. A1 could therefore satisfy predictions 1, 2 and 3 exactly while the title's causal claim is unsupported. Compounding this, 'collection policy, not content quality' is a false dichotomy on its face: collection policy has no channel to the bank except through written content, so the identifiable question is only correctness-gating versus diversity-gating — and the proposal's own arm B3 is a content-side diversity gate that is fairly likely to succeed, at which point refutation condition (iii) concedes the deployable recommendation and the paper reduces to 'gate for coverage, not correctness', which the memory-selection literature already does. Second blade: the regime (40-item seed, <=160 items, k=4, 65% draw skew) is admittedly chosen so contraction is 'measurable within three cycles', while the MDE arithmetic gives 5-6 points on the primary A1-vs-A2 tail contrast and 8-10 on the 2x2 interaction — larger than the effects the track's own prior measurements produced (full-bank injection broke 6-7 items; optimizer gains sat inside a 5-14 point re-scoring drift). The design is thus squeezed between power and ecological validity: a positive result shows a regime can be constructed in which the loop contracts, and a null at cycle 3 is uninformative by the authors' own limitation 1.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in priority order. (1) Add a memory-masked-distillation arm: episodes run fully coupled, but the retrieved items are stripped from the distiller's input. This is the arm that separates 'the episode was conditioned on retrieval' from 'the writer paraphrased what it was shown', and without it prong 1's causal claim is not identified. (2) Stratify the W=40 write sample by task cluster (or report cluster-conditional write rates and re-run the contraction metrics on a composition-matched subsample) so that contraction cannot be a pure success-rate selection effect under the skewed draw distribution. (3) Retitle and restate the claim to something the design can actually adjudicate — 'correctness-gated admission does not prevent support contraction; coverage-aware or decoupled collection does' — and treat B3 as a co-primary intervention rather than a threat, since it is the deployable one (A2 is not deployable: it discards memory during collection). (4) Fix the transplant test's confound: A3's and A4's instructions were evolved against different episode distributions, so any tail gap may be generic optimizer/trace quality, not co-adaptation to a contracted support. Add an arm where the optimizer evolves against memory-conditioned episodes over a *frozen* cycle-0 bank; only if A3's instruction underperforms *that* one on a healthy bank is co-adaptation to contraction demonstrated. Also cite and position against the recommender feedback-loop literature explicitly rather than only model collapse. Given the stated 8-10 point interaction MDE, either buy power for the 2x2 (more trajectories, or within-trajectory instruction swaps) or drop it from the abstract and make the corrected transplant the co-adaptation evidence.
missing_baseline: The coupled-collection / memory-masked-distillation arm (A1 with retrieved items removed from the distiller's context). Reviewers will demand it because it is the only arm that distinguishes preferential attachment through the agent's behaviour from the writer simply copying the text it was shown, and its absence means B2, B3, B1, F0 and M50 all leave the trivial explanation standing. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also raise: a cluster-stratified write-sampling arm (to kill the success-composition confound), and a coupled-instruction / frozen-bank arm (to make the transplant contrast interpretable as co-adaptation rather than trace quality).
preprint_collision: The check is well above average for this format and should be credited: it names a near-identical mechanistic premise (CoEvo-Mem), refuses to minimize it, converts it into a live outcome as baseline (ii), and flags honestly that it could not sweep OpenReview 2026 and that a memory-off collection ablation could sit in a sibling appendix. That is the right posture. Two real deficiencies remain. First, it reports conclusions but no protocol — no queries, no date windows, no venues, no indication of whether arXiv listings for the last 60-90 days were swept as opposed to keyword search — so 'the literature search run for this revision' is unauditable, and the field's fastest-moving surface (very recent preprints on retrieval-conditioned write-back) is exactly where the risk lives. Second, and more damaging, the search is scoped to agent-memory and model-collapse preprints and misses the older, non-preprint literature that already owns the claim: degenerate feedback loops and algorithmic-confounding homogenization in recommender systems (Jiang et al. AIES 2019; Chaney et al. RecSys 2018), where 'the policy that selects what is observed makes future observations reinforce it, contracting support' is a settled result with randomization/exploration as the established remedy. Likewise the mixing-ratio fix (M50) is presented as this proposal's one-line contribution, but accumulate-versus-replace results in the self-consuming-data line already predict it, and the proposal cites Shumailov and Alemohammad without engaging that specific finding. So: no exact scoop identified, but the novelty claim is narrower than the check concludes — the mechanism and the fix are both prior, and only the substrate and the prompt-optimizer crossing survive.
